190	def _render_one(job: tuple) -> dict | None:
191		menagerie, nominal, meta_path, out, k, seed, stride = job
192		meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
193		name = f"{meta['name']}_v{k:02d}.npz"
194		if (out / f"{name}.json").exists():  # finished by an earlier, interrupted run
195			return json.loads((out / f"{name}.json").read_text())
196		rng = np.random.default_rng([seed, int(meta["name"].split("_")[1]), k])
197		traj = np.load(meta_path.with_suffix(".npz"))
198		qpos = traj["qpos"]
199		phase = traj["phase"] if "phase" in traj.files else np.zeros(len(qpos), np.uint8)
200		lay = dict(meta["layout"])
201		# the gripper path close to the table (grasp, release) must stay in view; higher up it may leave the frame at the
202		# top edge as in the real recordings, and the show frames are checked separately below
203		showing = np.isin(phase, [PHASES.index("show_move"), PHASES.index("show_hold")])
204		low = traj["tcp"][(traj["tcp"][:, 2] < 0.06) & ~showing]
205		main = CameraPose(**meta["top_camera"]) if "top_camera" in meta else None
206		hold = np.flatnonzero(phase == PHASES.index("show_hold"))[::5]
207		layout = Layout(**{**lay, "top": main or nominal, "front": sample_front_camera(rng)})
208		layout.table_rgb = tuple(np.clip(np.array(lay["table_rgb"]) + rng.normal(0, 0.03, 3), 0.3, 0.85))
209		layout.light_level = float(rng.uniform(0.6, 1.0))
210		layout.light_dir = (float(rng.normal(0, 0.4)), float(rng.normal(0, 0.4)), -1.0)
211		cell = Cell(layout, menagerie)
212		# arm swept volume: collision geometry every 5th frame, as spheres of the geoms' bounding radii
213		swept, radii = [], []
214		for t in range(0, len(qpos), 5):
215			cell.data.qpos[:] = qpos[t]
216			mujoco.mj_kinematics(cell.model, cell.data)
217			swept.append(cell.data.geom_xpos[cell.robot_geoms].copy())
218			radii.append(cell.model.geom_rbound[cell.robot_geoms])
219		swept_pts, swept_r = np.vstack(swept), np.concatenate(radii)
220		rejected, why = 0, ""
221		top = None
222		for attempt in range(200):
223			cand = perturb_main_camera(rng, main) if main else sample_top_camera(rng, nominal)
224			if main and attempt >= 20:
225				cand = main  # the simulated camera passed these checks when the show poses were planned
226			ok, why = top_view_ok(cand, lay, low[:: max(1, len(low) // 40)])
227			if ok:
228				cell.set_camera("top", cand)
229				ok, why = _show_frames_ok(cell, qpos, hold, meta["defective"])
230			if ok:
231				top = cand
232				break
233			rejected += 1
234			if main and attempt >= 20:
235				break
236		if top is None:
237			logger.warning("%s view %d: no plausible main camera (%s)", meta["name"], k, why)
238			cell.renderer.close()
239			return None
240		targets = np.array([[*lay["brick_xy"], 0.02], [*lay["green"], BOWL_H], [*lay["pink"], BOWL_H]])
241		for _ in range(500):
242			side = sample_side_camera(rng)
243			ok, why = camera_view_ok(
244				np.array([side.x, side.y, side.height]), camera_forward(side), swept_pts, 0.05, radii=swept_r
245			)
246			uv, front = project(side, targets, (640, 480))
247			if ok and front.all() and np.all((uv > 20) & (uv < np.array([620, 460]))):
248				break
249			rejected += 1
250		else:
251			logger.warning("%s view %d: no side camera clears the arm (%s)", meta["name"], k, why)
252			cell.renderer.close()
253			return None
254		cell.set_camera("front", side)
255		frames = list(range(0, meta["length"], stride))
256		# preallocated: an episode is about 2 GB of frames, so a list plus a stacked copy would double the peak memory
257		cams = {c: np.empty((len(frames), *shape), np.uint8) for c, shape in CAMERA_SHAPES.items()}
258		defect_px = np.zeros(len(frames), np.int32)
259		brick_px = np.zeros(len(frames), np.int32)
260		for i, t in enumerate(frames):
261			cell.data.qpos[:] = qpos[t]
262			mujoco.mj_forward(cell.model, cell.data)
263			cams["top_rgb_v2"][i], cams["top_depth_v2"][i] = cell.top_images()
264			cams["front"][i] = cell.rgb("front")
265			cams["wrist"][i] = cell.rgb("wrist_cam")
266			vis = cell.visibility("top", TOP_CROP, full=False)
267			defect_px[i] = vis["defect"] if meta["defective"] else 0
268			brick_px[i] = vis["brick"]
269		cell.renderer.close()
270		np.savez_compressed(
271			out / name,
272			state=traj["state"][frames],
273			action=traj["action"][frames],
274			phase=phase[frames],
275			defect_px=defect_px,
276			brick_px=brick_px,
277			**cams,
278		)
279		logger.info("rendered %s (%d frames)", name, len(frames))
280		entry = {
281			"file": name,
282			"length": len(frames),
283			"success": True,
284			"task": meta["task"],
285			"defective": meta["defective"],
286			"defect_face": meta.get("defect_face"),
287			"presented": meta.get("presented", False),
288			"sim_episode": meta["name"],
289			"top_camera": asdict(top),
290			"front_camera": asdict(side),
291			"rejected_cameras": rejected,
292		}
293		(out / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(entry, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
294		return entry
295	
296	
297	def render_views(
298		menagerie: Path,
299		camera_file: Path,
300		sim_dir: Path,
301		out: Path,
302		views: int,
303		seed: int,
304		stride: int = 1,
305		workers: int = 1,
306	) -> dict:
307		"""Replay every successful simulated episode under ``views`` random plausible cameras and appearances.
308	
309		Writes the ``offline_pipeline`` format (``index.json`` + one ``.npz`` per rendered episode), which
310		``lerobot_export.py --video --robot-type SO101_Follower`` turns into a dataset shaped like sort-depth-v2.
311		Each finished episode also gets a ``.json`` entry, so rerunning into the same ``out`` resumes an interrupted run.
312		An episode holds about 2 GB of frames in memory while it renders: keep ``workers`` times 2 GB below the RAM.
313		"""
314		nominal = CameraPose(**json.loads(camera_file.read_text())["camera"])
315		out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
316		metas = [p for p in sorted(sim_dir.glob("sim_*.json")) if json.loads(p.read_text())["success"]]
317		jobs = [(menagerie, nominal, p, out, k, seed, stride) for p in metas for k in range(views)]
318		if workers <= 1:
319			results = [_render_one(j) for j in jobs]
320		else:
321			with _pool(workers) as pool:
322				results = list(pool.map(_render_one, jobs))
323		episodes = [r for r in results if r is not None]
324		index = {
325			"fps": FPS // stride,
326			"state_names": STATE_NAMES,
327			"cameras": CAMERA_SHAPES,
328			"source": "mujoco-sim",
329			"privileged": {
330				"phase": "per-frame expert phase, index into phases",
331				"phases": list(PHASES),
332				"defect_px": "defect pixels visible in top_rgb_v2 (segmentation render; 0 for a normal brick)",
333				"brick_px": "brick pixels visible in top_rgb_v2",
334			},
335			"menagerie_commit": "370c43965323c0944b433b202aac5058b5f907a9",
336			"episodes": episodes,
337			"rejected_cameras": sum(r["rejected_cameras"] for r in episodes),
338		}
339		(out / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
340		return index
341

"""Episode generation: simulate once (physics, full 3D state per frame), then render many views of each episode."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from dataclasses import asdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from ..camera import CameraPose, camera_forward, project
from ..constants import BOWL_H, BOWL_R, CAMERA_SHAPES, FPS, PHASES, STATE_NAMES, TASKS, TOP_CROP
from ..joints import normalized_to_rad, rad_to_normalized
from ..presentation import FACES, camera_view_ok, show_points
from ._mj import mujoco
from .cell import Cell
from .expert import (
	SHOW_DISTANCES_M,
	SHOW_OFF_AXIS_DEG,
	SHOW_REACH_M,
	SHOW_Z_MIN_M,
	Plan,
	expert_handoff,
	expert_pick,
	expert_place,
	expert_present,
	presentation_search,
)
from .layout import Layout, sample_layout
from .views import perturb_main_camera, sample_front_camera, sample_side_camera, sample_top_camera, top_view_ok

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _simulate_one(job: tuple) -> dict:
	menagerie, nominal, prior, out, e, seed, rest_u = job
	rng = np.random.default_rng([seed, e])
	rest = normalized_to_rad(rest_u)
	defective = bool(rng.random() < 0.35)
	for _ in range(500):
		layout = sample_layout(rng, nominal, defective, prior)
		if top_view_ok(nominal, asdict(layout), np.zeros((0, 3)), margin_px=30.0)[0]:
			break
	else:
		raise RuntimeError("no layout fits the nominal top camera; check the camera file")
	# The main (inspection) camera is fixed before simulating: the presentation poses are planned against it, and
	# rendering only perturbs it slightly. A camera without a reachable show point is rejected.
	layout.defect_face = int(rng.integers(len(FACES)))
	for _ in range(50):
		main = sample_top_camera(rng, nominal)
		cam = np.array([main.x, main.y, main.height])
		pts = show_points(cam, camera_forward(main), SHOW_DISTANCES_M, SHOW_OFF_AXIS_DEG, SHOW_REACH_M, SHOW_Z_MIN_M)
		if len(pts) and top_view_ok(main, asdict(layout), np.zeros((0, 3)), margin_px=20.0)[0]:
			break
	else:
		raise RuntimeError("no main camera near the nominal one has a reachable show point")
	layout.top = main
	start = rest + np.concatenate([rng.normal(0, 0.05, 5), [0.0]])
	cell = Cell(layout, menagerie)
	cell.set_joints(start)
	qpos, state, action, tcp, phase = [], [], [], [], []

	def run(plan: Plan, first: int) -> None:
		for target, ph in zip(plan.frames[first:], plan.phases[first:], strict=True):
			noisy = target + np.concatenate([rng.normal(0, 0.004, 5), [0.0]])
			qpos.append(cell.data.qpos.copy())
			state.append(rad_to_normalized(cell.joints()))
			action.append(rad_to_normalized(noisy))
			tcp.append(cell.data.site_xpos[cell.site].copy())
			phase.append(ph)
			cell.step(noisy)
			cell.update_grasp(float(target[5]))

	plan, grip = expert_pick(cell, start, rng)
	run(plan, 0)
	grasped = cell.held is not None
	shown: list[dict] = []
	search: dict = {"show_point": None, "poses": [], "points_tried": 0}
	if grasped:
		n = len(plan.frames)
		search = presentation_search(cell, cell.joints(), main)
		shown = expert_present(plan, search, rng, grip.closed_g)
		expert_handoff(cell, plan, grip, rng)
		run(plan, n)
	n = len(plan.frames)
	expert_place(cell, plan, grip, start)
	run(plan, n)
	bowl = np.array(layout.pink if defective else layout.green)
	brick = cell.brick_pos()
	success = bool(np.hypot(*(brick[:2] - bowl)) < BOWL_R and brick[2] < 0.05)
	name = f"sim_{e:04d}"
	np.savez_compressed(
		out / f"{name}.npz",
		qpos=np.array(qpos),
		state=np.array(state, np.float32),
		action=np.array(action, np.float32),
		tcp=np.array(tcp),
		phase=np.array(phase, np.uint8),
	)
	entry = {
		"name": name,
		"length": len(plan.frames),
		"success": success,
		"grasped": grasped,
		"presented": bool(shown),
		"final_brick": brick.tolist(),
		"task": TASKS["pink" if defective else "green"],
		"defective": defective,
		"defect_face": layout.defect_face,
		"phases": list(PHASES),
		"top_camera": asdict(main),
		"presentation": {
			"show_point": search["show_point"],
			"points_tried": search["points_tried"],
			"poses_scored": len(search["poses"]),
			"shown": shown,
		},
		"layout": {k: v for k, v in asdict(layout).items() if k not in ("top", "front")},
	}
	(out / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(entry, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
	cell.renderer.close()
	logger.info(
		"simulated %s: %d frames, %s bowl, face %d, grasped=%s, shown=%d poses (best %.0f px), success=%s",
		name,
		len(plan.frames),
		"pink" if defective else "green",
		layout.defect_face,
		grasped,
		len(shown),
		shown[0]["defect"] if shown else 0,
		success,
	)
	return entry


def _log_setup() -> None:
	logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")


def _pool(workers: int):
	import multiprocessing
	from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

	return ProcessPoolExecutor(workers, mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"), initializer=_log_setup)


def simulate(
	menagerie: Path,
	camera_file: Path,
	out: Path,
	episodes: int,
	seed: int,
	rest_u: np.ndarray,
	prior_file: Path | None = None,
	workers: int = 1,
) -> list[dict]:
	"""Run scripted episodes with physics grasping; store full 3D state per frame (qpos), actions and the layout.

	Episode ``e`` draws everything from ``default_rng([seed, e])``, so results do not depend on ``workers``.
	"""
	nominal = CameraPose(**json.loads(camera_file.read_text())["camera"])
	prior = [p for p in json.loads(prior_file.read_text()) if "green" in p and "pink" in p] if prior_file else None
	out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
	jobs = [(menagerie, nominal, prior, out, e, seed, rest_u) for e in range(episodes)]
	if workers <= 1:
		return [_simulate_one(j) for j in jobs]
	with _pool(workers) as pool:
		return list(pool.map(_simulate_one, jobs))


def _show_frames_ok(cell: Cell, qpos: np.ndarray, frames: np.ndarray, defective: bool) -> tuple[bool, str]:
	"""In the sampled show-hold frames the brick is inside the crop and at least half unoccluded, and a defective
	brick shows its defect in at least one of them."""
	if len(frames) == 0:
		return True, ""
	seen = 0
	for t in frames:
		cell.data.qpos[:] = qpos[t]
		mujoco.mj_forward(cell.model, cell.data)
		vis = cell.visibility("top", TOP_CROP)
		if vis["brick_full"] < 50 or vis["brick"] < 0.5 * vis["brick_full"]:
			return False, f"brick occluded or outside the crop at frame {t}"
		seen += vis["defect"]
	if defective and seen == 0:
		return False, "defect never visible in the show frames"
	return True, ""


def _render_one(job: tuple) -> dict | None:
	menagerie, nominal, meta_path, out, k, seed, stride = job
	meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
	name = f"{meta['name']}_v{k:02d}.npz"
	if (out / f"{name}.json").exists():  # finished by an earlier, interrupted run
		return json.loads((out / f"{name}.json").read_text())
	rng = np.random.default_rng([seed, int(meta["name"].split("_")[1]), k])
	traj = np.load(meta_path.with_suffix(".npz"))
	qpos = traj["qpos"]
	phase = traj["phase"] if "phase" in traj.files else np.zeros(len(qpos), np.uint8)
	lay = dict(meta["layout"])
	# the gripper path close to the table (grasp, release) must stay in view; higher up it may leave the frame at the
	# top edge as in the real recordings, and the show frames are checked separately below
	showing = np.isin(phase, [PHASES.index("show_move"), PHASES.index("show_hold")])
	low = traj["tcp"][(traj["tcp"][:, 2] < 0.06) & ~showing]
	main = CameraPose(**meta["top_camera"]) if "top_camera" in meta else None
	hold = np.flatnonzero(phase == PHASES.index("show_hold"))[::5]
	layout = Layout(**{**lay, "top": main or nominal, "front": sample_front_camera(rng)})
	layout.table_rgb = tuple(np.clip(np.array(lay["table_rgb"]) + rng.normal(0, 0.03, 3), 0.3, 0.85))
	layout.light_level = float(rng.uniform(0.6, 1.0))
	layout.light_dir = (float(rng.normal(0, 0.4)), float(rng.normal(0, 0.4)), -1.0)
	cell = Cell(layout, menagerie)
	# arm swept volume: collision geometry every 5th frame, as spheres of the geoms' bounding radii
	swept, radii = [], []
	for t in range(0, len(qpos), 5):
		cell.data.qpos[:] = qpos[t]
		mujoco.mj_kinematics(cell.model, cell.data)
		swept.append(cell.data.geom_xpos[cell.robot_geoms].copy())
		radii.append(cell.model.geom_rbound[cell.robot_geoms])
	swept_pts, swept_r = np.vstack(swept), np.concatenate(radii)
	rejected, why = 0, ""
	top = None
	for attempt in range(200):
		cand = perturb_main_camera(rng, main) if main else sample_top_camera(rng, nominal)
		if main and attempt >= 20:
			cand = main  # the simulated camera passed these checks when the show poses were planned
		ok, why = top_view_ok(cand, lay, low[:: max(1, len(low) // 40)])
		if ok:
			cell.set_camera("top", cand)
			ok, why = _show_frames_ok(cell, qpos, hold, meta["defective"])
		if ok:
			top = cand
			break
		rejected += 1
		if main and attempt >= 20:
			break
	if top is None:
		logger.warning("%s view %d: no plausible main camera (%s)", meta["name"], k, why)
		cell.renderer.close()
		return None
	targets = np.array([[*lay["brick_xy"], 0.02], [*lay["green"], BOWL_H], [*lay["pink"], BOWL_H]])
	for _ in range(500):
		side = sample_side_camera(rng)
		ok, why = camera_view_ok(
			np.array([side.x, side.y, side.height]), camera_forward(side), swept_pts, 0.05, radii=swept_r
		)
		uv, front = project(side, targets, (640, 480))
		if ok and front.all() and np.all((uv > 20) & (uv < np.array([620, 460]))):
			break
		rejected += 1
	else:
		logger.warning("%s view %d: no side camera clears the arm (%s)", meta["name"], k, why)
		cell.renderer.close()
		return None
	cell.set_camera("front", side)
	frames = list(range(0, meta["length"], stride))
	# preallocated: an episode is about 2 GB of frames, so a list plus a stacked copy would double the peak memory
	cams = {c: np.empty((len(frames), *shape), np.uint8) for c, shape in CAMERA_SHAPES.items()}
	defect_px = np.zeros(len(frames), np.int32)
	brick_px = np.zeros(len(frames), np.int32)
	for i, t in enumerate(frames):
		cell.data.qpos[:] = qpos[t]
		mujoco.mj_forward(cell.model, cell.data)
		cams["top_rgb_v2"][i], cams["top_depth_v2"][i] = cell.top_images()
		cams["front"][i] = cell.rgb("front")
		cams["wrist"][i] = cell.rgb("wrist_cam")
		vis = cell.visibility("top", TOP_CROP, full=False)
		defect_px[i] = vis["defect"] if meta["defective"] else 0
		brick_px[i] = vis["brick"]
	cell.renderer.close()
	np.savez_compressed(
		out / name,
		state=traj["state"][frames],
		action=traj["action"][frames],
		phase=phase[frames],
		defect_px=defect_px,
		brick_px=brick_px,
		**cams,
	)
	logger.info("rendered %s (%d frames)", name, len(frames))
	entry = {
		"file": name,
		"length": len(frames),
		"success": True,
		"task": meta["task"],
		"defective": meta["defective"],
		"defect_face": meta.get("defect_face"),
		"presented": meta.get("presented", False),
		"sim_episode": meta["name"],
		"top_camera": asdict(top),
		"front_camera": asdict(side),
		"rejected_cameras": rejected,
	}
	(out / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(entry, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
	return entry


def render_views(
	menagerie: Path,
	camera_file: Path,
	sim_dir: Path,
	out: Path,
	views: int,
	seed: int,
	stride: int = 1,
	workers: int = 1,
) -> dict:
	"""Replay every successful simulated episode under ``views`` random plausible cameras and appearances.

	Writes the ``offline_pipeline`` format (``index.json`` + one ``.npz`` per rendered episode), which
	``lerobot_export.py --video --robot-type SO101_Follower`` turns into a dataset shaped like sort-depth-v2.
	Each finished episode also gets a ``.json`` entry, so rerunning into the same ``out`` resumes an interrupted run.
	An episode holds about 2 GB of frames in memory while it renders: keep ``workers`` times 2 GB below the RAM.
	"""
	nominal = CameraPose(**json.loads(camera_file.read_text())["camera"])
	out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
	metas = [p for p in sorted(sim_dir.glob("sim_*.json")) if json.loads(p.read_text())["success"]]
	jobs = [(menagerie, nominal, p, out, k, seed, stride) for p in metas for k in range(views)]
	if workers <= 1:
		results = [_render_one(j) for j in jobs]
	else:
		with _pool(workers) as pool:
			results = list(pool.map(_render_one, jobs))
	episodes = [r for r in results if r is not None]
	index = {
		"fps": FPS // stride,
		"state_names": STATE_NAMES,
		"cameras": CAMERA_SHAPES,
		"source": "mujoco-sim",
		"privileged": {
			"phase": "per-frame expert phase, index into phases",
			"phases": list(PHASES),
			"defect_px": "defect pixels visible in top_rgb_v2 (segmentation render; 0 for a normal brick)",
			"brick_px": "brick pixels visible in top_rgb_v2",
		},
		"menagerie_commit": "370c43965323c0944b433b202aac5058b5f907a9",
		"episodes": episodes,
		"rejected_cameras": sum(r["rejected_cameras"] for r in episodes),
	}
	(out / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
	return index

"""The optional ``mujoco`` import, with a headless GL backend selected where one is needed.

On Linux (WSL2 on the training PC: ``MESA_D3D12_DEFAULT_ADAPTER_NAME=NVIDIA``) offscreen rendering needs
``MUJOCO_GL=egl``; MuJoCo rejects that value on Windows and macOS, where its default backend already renders
offscreen. An explicit ``MUJOCO_GL`` in the environment always wins. ``mujoco`` is ``None`` when the package is not
installed, so the scene and layout code stays importable for the hardware-free tests.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import platform

if platform.system() == "Linux":
	os.environ.setdefault("MUJOCO_GL", "egl")
try:
	import mujoco
except ModuleNotFoundError:
	mujoco = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

__all__ = ["mujoco"]

112	def _build_mj_pick_place_plan(spec, cond, top_cam: CameraPose, seed: int = 0):
113		"""Solve MuJoCo IK plan for a pick-show-place condition (returns trajectory, phases, q_start)."""
114		from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import (
115			Cell,
116			Grip,
117			Plan,
118			best_roll,
119			expert_handoff,
120			ik,
121			ik_reach,
122			release_point,
123		)
124	
125		size = BRICK_SIZES[cond.brick_size]

127			brick_xy=cond.brick_xy,
128			yaw_deg=cond.brick_yaw_deg,
129			size=size,
130			clutter_per_bowl=cond.clutter_per_bowl,
131			seed=seed,
132		)
133		lay.top = top_cam
134		cell = Cell(
135			lay,
136			SO101_MJCF_DIR,
137			physics=spec,
138			dynamic_clutter=True,
139			assisted_grasp=False,
140			mass_scale=cond.mass_scale,
141			friction_scale=cond.friction_scale,
142			render_enabled=False,
143		)
144		q_start = normalized_to_rad(np.array(REST_U, dtype=np.float64))
145		q_start[5] = OPEN_G
146		cell.set_joints(q_start)
147	
148		bx, by = lay.brick_xy
149		yaw = math.radians(lay.brick_yaw_deg)
150		short_axis = np.array([-math.sin(yaw), math.cos(yaw)])
151		q_hover = ik(cell, np.array([bx, by, 0.09]), q_start.copy(), 0.0)
152		roll, sign = best_roll(cell, q_hover, short_axis)
153		grip = Grip(roll, open_g=OPEN_G, closed_g=HOLD_G)
154		offset = -sign * short_axis * (size[1] / 2.0 + 0.006)
155		gx, gy = bx + offset[0], by + offset[1]
156		z_grip = 0.006
157		plan = Plan(q_start, 1.0)
158		plan.hold(0.3, "rest")
159		q = np.array([0.0, -0.35, 0.25, 1.35, 0.0, grip.open_g], dtype=np.float64)
160		plan.move(q, 0.8, "approach")
161		for x, y, z, g, secs, phase in (
162			(gx, gy, 0.09, grip.open_g, 1.4, "approach"),
163			(gx, gy, z_grip + 0.02, grip.open_g, 1.2, "approach"),
164			(gx, gy, z_grip, grip.open_g, 0.7, "grasp"),
165			(gx, gy, z_grip, grip.closed_g, 1.0, "grasp"),
166			(gx, gy, 0.12, grip.closed_g, 1.2, "lift"),
167		):
168			q = ik(cell, np.array([x, y, z]), q, roll)
169			q[5] = g
170			plan.move(q, secs, phase)
171		grip.q_lift = q.copy()
172	
173		for wr_deg in (-35.0, 0.0, 35.0):
174			q_show = q.copy()
175			q_show[3] = 0.65
176			q_show[4] = math.radians(wr_deg)
177			q_show[5] = HOLD_G
178			plan.move(q_show, 0.65, "show_move", settle=0.0)

PINK_XY = (0.26, -0.18)


def _git_head() -> str | None:
	try:
		out = subprocess.run(
			["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
			check=True,
			capture_output=True,
			text=True,
		)
		return out.stdout.strip()
	except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError):
		return None


def _mj_brick_layout(
	brick_xy: tuple[float, float] = (0.26, 0.0),
	yaw_deg: float = 0.0,
	size: tuple[float, float, float] = DUPLO_2X2,
	clutter_per_bowl: int = 0,
	seed: int = 0,
):
	from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import Layout

	rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
	clutter = []
	for bowl in (GREEN_XY, PINK_XY):
		for _ in range(clutter_per_bowl):
			r = BOWL_R * 0.55 * math.sqrt(float(rng.random()))
			a = float(rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0 * math.pi))
			clutter.append(
				(
					bowl[0] + r * math.cos(a),
					bowl[1] + r * math.sin(a),
					float(rng.uniform(0.0, math.pi)),
					0.1,
					0.42,
					0.80,
				)
			)
	return Layout(
		green=GREEN_XY,
		pink=PINK_XY,
		brick_xy=brick_xy,
		brick_yaw_deg=yaw_deg,
		defective=True,
		brick_size=size,
		clutter=clutter,
	)


def _build_mj_pick_place_plan(spec, cond, top_cam: CameraPose, seed: int = 0):
	"""Solve MuJoCo IK plan for a pick-show-place condition (returns trajectory, phases, q_start)."""
	from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import (
		Cell,
		Grip,
		Plan,
		best_roll,
		expert_handoff,
		ik,
		ik_reach,
		release_point,
	)

	size = BRICK_SIZES[cond.brick_size]
	lay = _mj_brick_layout(
		brick_xy=cond.brick_xy,
		yaw_deg=cond.brick_yaw_deg,
		size=size,
		clutter_per_bowl=cond.clutter_per_bowl,
		seed=seed,
	)
	lay.top = top_cam
	cell = Cell(
		lay,
		SO101_MJCF_DIR,
		physics=spec,
		dynamic_clutter=True,
		assisted_grasp=False,
		mass_scale=cond.mass_scale,
		friction_scale=cond.friction_scale,
		render_enabled=False,
	)
	q_start = normalized_to_rad(np.array(REST_U, dtype=np.float64))
	q_start[5] = OPEN_G
	cell.set_joints(q_start)

	bx, by = lay.brick_xy
	yaw = math.radians(lay.brick_yaw_deg)
	short_axis = np.array([-math.sin(yaw), math.cos(yaw)])
	q_hover = ik(cell, np.array([bx, by, 0.09]), q_start.copy(), 0.0)
	roll, sign = best_roll(cell, q_hover, short_axis)
	grip = Grip(roll, open_g=OPEN_G, closed_g=HOLD_G)
	offset = -sign * short_axis * (size[1] / 2.0 + 0.006)
	gx, gy = bx + offset[0], by + offset[1]
	z_grip = 0.006
	plan = Plan(q_start, 1.0)
	plan.hold(0.3, "rest")
	q = np.array([0.0, -0.35, 0.25, 1.35, 0.0, grip.open_g], dtype=np.float64)
	plan.move(q, 0.8, "approach")
	for x, y, z, g, secs, phase in (
		(gx, gy, 0.09, grip.open_g, 1.4, "approach"),
		(gx, gy, z_grip + 0.02, grip.open_g, 1.2, "approach"),
		(gx, gy, z_grip, grip.open_g, 0.7, "grasp"),
		(gx, gy, z_grip, grip.closed_g, 1.0, "grasp"),
		(gx, gy, 0.12, grip.closed_g, 1.2, "lift"),
	):
		q = ik(cell, np.array([x, y, z]), q, roll)
		q[5] = g
		plan.move(q, secs, phase)
	grip.q_lift = q.copy()

	for wr_deg in (-35.0, 0.0, 35.0):
		q_show = q.copy()
		q_show[3] = 0.65
		q_show[4] = math.radians(wr_deg)
		q_show[5] = HOLD_G
		plan.move(q_show, 0.65, "show_move", settle=0.0)
		plan.hold(0.35, "show_hold")
	expert_handoff(cell, plan, grip, np.random.default_rng(seed))

	bowl_xy = lay.pink if lay.defective else lay.green
	rp = release_point(bowl_xy)
	q_pl = grip.q_lift.copy()
	for z, g, secs in ((0.12, HOLD_G, 1.8), (0.065, HOLD_G, 1.2), (0.065, OPEN_G, 0.6), (0.12, OPEN_G, 0.8)):
		q_pl = ik_reach(cell, np.array([rp[0], rp[1], z]), q_pl, grip.roll)
		q_pl[5] = g
		plan.move(q_pl, secs, "place")
	plan.move(q_start.copy(), 1.2, "return")
	plan.hold(0.9, "return")
	cell.close()
	return np.array(plan.frames, dtype=np.float64), np.array(plan.phases, dtype=np.uint8), q_start, bowl_xy


def _mj_step_trajectory(
	cell,
	q_targets: np.ndarray,
	q_start: np.ndarray,
	brick_xy: tuple[float, float] = (0.26, 0.0),
	brick_yaw_deg: float = 0.0,
	non_ideal: NonIdealityCfg | None = None,
) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
	"""Run an open-loop joint target sequence in pure-physics MuJoCo at 240 Hz with substep telemetry."""
	from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell._mj import mujoco

	cell.model.opt.timestep = 1.0 / PHYSICS_HZ
	cell.set_joints(q_start)
	cell.data.qvel[:] = 0.0
	yaw_rad = math.radians(brick_yaw_deg)
	b_quat = (0.0, 0.0, math.sin(yaw_rad / 2.0), math.cos(yaw_rad / 2.0))
	cell.set_brick_pose(
		np.array([brick_xy[0], brick_xy[1], cell.layout.brick_size[2] / 2.0 + 0.0005]), np.array(b_quat)
	)
	cell.data.ctrl[:6] = q_start
	for _ in range(12):
		mujoco.mj_step(cell.model, cell.data)

	filt = ActuatorCommandFilter(non_ideal, n_joints=6, fps=FPS) if non_ideal is not None else None
	if filt is not None:
		filt.reset(q_start)

	qcmd_log, qpos_log, tcp_log, eeq_log = [], [], [], []
	bpos_log, bquat_log, bvel_log, bang_log = [], [], [], []
	jaw_log, jaw_n_log, jaw_t_log, unint_log, sub_unint_log, tq_log = [], [], [], [], [], []

	for target in q_targets:
		q_cmd = filt.step_command(target, cell.joints()) if filt is not None else target
		sub = cell.step_with_telemetry(q_cmd, substeps=SUBSTEPS)
		qcmd_log.append(q_cmd.copy())
		qpos_log.append(cell.joints())
		tcp_log.append(cell.tcp_pos())
		wxyz = cell.data.xquat[cell.grip_body]
		eeq_log.append(np.array([wxyz[1], wxyz[2], wxyz[3], wxyz[0]], dtype=np.float64))
		bpos_log.append(cell.brick_pos())
		bquat_log.append(cell.brick_quat_xyzw())
		lv, av = cell.brick_vel()
		bvel_log.append(lv)
		bang_log.append(av)
		jaw_log.append(sub["jaw_total"][-1])
		jaw_n_log.append(sub["jaw_normal"].mean(axis=1))
		jaw_t_log.append(sub["jaw_tangential"].mean(axis=1))
		unint_log.append(float(sub["unintended"][-1]))
		sub_unint_log.append(sub["unintended"])
		tq_log.append(sub["torques"][np.argmax(np.abs(sub["torques"]), axis=0), np.arange(6)])

	return {
		"t": np.arange(len(q_targets), dtype=np.float64) / float(FPS),
		"q_cmd": np.array(qcmd_log),
		"qpos": np.array(qpos_log),
		"tcp_pos": np.array(tcp_log),
		"ee_quat": np.array(eeq_log),
		"brick_pos": np.array(bpos_log),
		"brick_quat": np.array(bquat_log),
		"brick_vel": np.array(bvel_log),
		"brick_ang_vel": np.array(bang_log),
		"jaw_forces": np.array(jaw_log),
		"pinch_normal": np.array(jaw_n_log),
		"pinch_tangential": np.array(jaw_t_log),
		"unintended_forces": np.array(unint_log),
		"substep_unintended": np.array(sub_unint_log),
		"actuator_torques": np.array(tq_log),
	}


def _evaluate_mj_rollout(res: dict[str, np.ndarray], phases: np.ndarray, spec, size, bowl_xy) -> dict[str, Any]:
	torque_lims = np.array([spec.arm_actuator.effort_limit] * 5 + [spec.gripper_actuator.effort_limit])
	health = evaluate_episode_health(
		q_cmd=res["q_cmd"],
		q_act=res["qpos"],
		tcp_pos=res["tcp_pos"],
		brick_pos=res["brick_pos"],
		brick_quat=res["brick_quat"],
		jaw_forces=res["jaw_forces"],
		unintended_forces=res["unintended_forces"],
		phases=phases,
		target_bowl_xy=bowl_xy,
		bowl_r=BOWL_R,
		brick_vel=res["brick_vel"],
		brick_ang_vel=res["brick_ang_vel"],
		ee_quat=res["ee_quat"],
		fps=FPS,
		brick_size=size,
		substep_unintended_forces=res["substep_unintended"],
		pinch_normal_forces=res["pinch_normal"],
		pinch_tangential_forces=res["pinch_tangential"],
		actuator_torques=res["actuator_torques"],
		torque_limits=torque_lims,
		torque_source="solver_measured",
		timestamps=res["t"],
	)
	return health.to_dict()


def _mj_run_matrix_condition(cond, spec, top_cam: CameraPose, seed: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]:
	"""Run one pure-physics pick-show-place episode in MuJoCo for ``cond`` and ``seed``."""
	from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import Cell

	rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
	# Small reproducible pose jitter per seed when seed > 0 to span search & held-out placement sensitivity
	dx = float(rng.normal(0.0, 0.008)) if seed > 0 else 0.0
	dy = float(rng.normal(0.0, 0.008)) if seed > 0 else 0.0
	dyaw = float(rng.normal(0.0, 6.0)) if seed > 0 else 0.0
	cond_j = type(cond)(
		name=cond.name,
		brick_size=cond.brick_size,
		brick_xy=(cond.brick_xy[0] + dx, cond.brick_xy[1] + dy),
		brick_yaw_deg=cond.brick_yaw_deg + dyaw,
		defective=cond.defective,
		clutter_per_bowl=cond.clutter_per_bowl,
		mass_scale=cond.mass_scale,
		friction_scale=cond.friction_scale,
		latency_frames=cond.latency_frames,
		backlash_deg=cond.backlash_deg,
	)

	q_plan, phases, q_start, bowl_xy = _build_mj_pick_place_plan(spec, cond_j, top_cam, seed=seed)
	size = BRICK_SIZES[cond_j.brick_size]
	lay = _mj_brick_layout(
		brick_xy=cond_j.brick_xy,
		yaw_deg=cond_j.brick_yaw_deg,
		size=size,
		clutter_per_bowl=cond_j.clutter_per_bowl,
		seed=seed,
	)
	lay.top = top_cam
	cell = Cell(
		lay,
		SO101_MJCF_DIR,
		physics=spec,
		dynamic_clutter=True,
		assisted_grasp=False,
		mass_scale=cond_j.mass_scale,
		friction_scale=cond_j.friction_scale,
		render_enabled=False,
	)
	non_ideal = NonIdealityCfg(
		latency_frames=cond_j.latency_frames,
		backlash_rad=math.radians(cond_j.backlash_deg),
		velocity_limit_rad_s=spec.arm_actuator.velocity_limit,
		encoder_ticks=4096,
	)
	res = _mj_step_trajectory(
		cell,
		q_plan,
		q_start,
		brick_xy=cond_j.brick_xy,
		brick_yaw_deg=cond_j.brick_yaw_deg,
		non_ideal=non_ideal,
	)
	cell.close()
	return _evaluate_mj_rollout(res, phases, spec, size, bowl_xy)


def _quat_yaw(quat_xyzw: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
	from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation

	return np.array([Rotation.from_quat(q).as_euler("xyz")[2] for q in quat_xyzw], dtype=np.float64)

112	def _build_mj_pick_place_plan(spec, cond, top_cam: CameraPose, seed: int = 0):
113		"""Solve MuJoCo IK plan for a pick-show-place condition (returns trajectory, phases, q_start)."""
114		from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import (
115			Cell,
116			Grip,
117			Plan,
118			best_roll,
119			expert_handoff,
120			ik,
121			ik_reach,
122			release_point,
123		)
124	
125		size = BRICK_SIZES[cond.brick_size]
126		lay = _mj_brick_layout(
127			brick_xy=cond.brick_xy,
128			yaw_deg=cond.brick_yaw_deg,
129			size=size,
130			clutter_per_bowl=cond.clutter_per_bowl,
131			seed=seed,
132		)
133		lay.top = top_cam
134		cell = Cell(
135			lay,
136			SO101_MJCF_DIR,
137			physics=spec,
138			dynamic_clutter=True,
139			assisted_grasp=False,
140			mass_scale=cond.mass_scale,
141			friction_scale=cond.friction_scale,
142			render_enabled=False,
143		)
144		q_start = normalized_to_rad(np.array(REST_U, dtype=np.float64))
145		q_start[5] = OPEN_G
146		cell.set_joints(q_start)
147	
148		bx, by = lay.brick_xy
149		yaw = math.radians(lay.brick_yaw_deg)
150		short_axis = np.array([-math.sin(yaw), math.cos(yaw)])
151		q_hover = ik(cell, np.array([bx, by, 0.09]), q_start.copy(), 0.0)
152		roll, sign = best_roll(cell, q_hover, short_axis)
153		grip = Grip(roll, open_g=OPEN_G, closed_g=HOLD_G)
154		offset = -sign * short_axis * (size[1] / 2.0 + 0.006)
155		gx, gy = bx + offset[0], by + offset[1]
156		z_grip = 0.006
157		plan = Plan(q_start, 1.0)
158		plan.hold(0.3, "rest")
159		q = np.array([0.0, -0.35, 0.25, 1.35, 0.0, grip.open_g], dtype=np.float64)
160		plan.move(q, 0.8, "approach")
161		for x, y, z, g, secs, phase in (
162			(gx, gy, 0.09, grip.open_g, 1.4, "approach"),
163			(gx, gy, z_grip + 0.02, grip.open_g, 1.2, "approach"),
164			(gx, gy, z_grip, grip.open_g, 0.7, "grasp"),
165			(gx, gy, z_grip, grip.closed_g, 1.0, "grasp"),
166			(gx, gy, 0.12, grip.closed_g, 1.2, "lift"),
167		):
168			q = ik(cell, np.array([x, y, z]), q, roll)
169			q[5] = g
170			plan.move(q, secs, phase)
171		grip.q_lift = q.copy()
172	
173		for wr_deg in (-35.0, 0.0, 35.0):
174			q_show = q.copy()
175			q_show[3] = 0.65
176			q_show[4] = math.radians(wr_deg)
177			q_show[5] = HOLD_G
178			plan.move(q_show, 0.65, "show_move", settle=0.0)
179			plan.hold(0.35, "show_hold")
180		expert_handoff(cell, plan, grip, np.random.default_rng(seed))
181	
182		bowl_xy = lay.pink if lay.defective else lay.green
183		rp = release_point(bowl_xy)
184		q_pl = grip.q_lift.copy()
185		for z, g, secs in ((0.12, HOLD_G, 1.8), (0.065, HOLD_G, 1.2), (0.065, OPEN_G, 0.6), (0.12, OPEN_G, 0.8)):
186			q_pl = ik_reach(cell, np.array([rp[0], rp[1], z]), q_pl, grip.roll)
187			q_pl[5] = g
188			plan.move(q_pl, secs, "place")
189		plan.move(q_start.copy(), 1.2, "return")
190		plan.hold(0.9, "return")

192		return np.array(plan.frames, dtype=np.float64), np.array(plan.phases, dtype=np.uint8), q_start, bowl_xy

195	def _mj_step_trajectory(
196		cell,
197		q_targets: np.ndarray,
198		q_start: np.ndarray,
199		brick_xy: tuple[float, float] = (0.26, 0.0),
200		brick_yaw_deg: float = 0.0,
201		non_ideal: NonIdealityCfg | None = None,
202	) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
203		"""Run an open-loop joint target sequence in pure-physics MuJoCo at 240 Hz with substep telemetry."""
204		from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell._mj import mujoco
205	
206		cell.model.opt.timestep = 1.0 / PHYSICS_HZ
207		cell.set_joints(q_start)
208		cell.data.qvel[:] = 0.0
209		yaw_rad = math.radians(brick_yaw_deg)
210		b_quat = (0.0, 0.0, math.sin(yaw_rad / 2.0), math.cos(yaw_rad / 2.0))
211		cell.set_brick_pose(
212			np.array([brick_xy[0], brick_xy[1], cell.layout.brick_size[2] / 2.0 + 0.0005]), np.array(b_quat)
213		)
214		cell.data.ctrl[:6] = q_start
215		for _ in range(12):
216			mujoco.mj_step(cell.model, cell.data)
217	
218		filt = ActuatorCommandFilter(non_ideal, n_joints=6, fps=FPS) if non_ideal is not None else None
219		if filt is not None:
220			filt.reset(q_start)
221	
222		qcmd_log, qpos_log, tcp_log, eeq_log = [], [], [], []
223		bpos_log, bquat_log, bvel_log, bang_log = [], [], [], []
224		jaw_log, jaw_n_log, jaw_t_log, unint_log, sub_unint_log, tq_log = [], [], [], [], [], []
225	
226		for target in q_targets:
227			q_cmd = filt.step_command(target, cell.joints()) if filt is not None else target
228			sub = cell.step_with_telemetry(q_cmd, substeps=SUBSTEPS)
229			qcmd_log.append(q_cmd.copy())
230			qpos_log.append(cell.joints())
231			tcp_log.append(cell.tcp_pos())
232			wxyz = cell.data.xquat[cell.grip_body]
233			eeq_log.append(np.array([wxyz[1], wxyz[2], wxyz[3], wxyz[0]], dtype=np.float64))
234			bpos_log.append(cell.brick_pos())
235			bquat_log.append(cell.brick_quat_xyzw())
236			lv, av = cell.brick_vel()
237			bvel_log.append(lv)
238			bang_log.append(av)
239			jaw_log.append(sub["jaw_total"][-1])
240			jaw_n_log.append(sub["jaw_normal"].mean(axis=1))
241			jaw_t_log.append(sub["jaw_tangential"].mean(axis=1))
242			unint_log.append(float(sub["unintended"][-1]))
243			sub_unint_log.append(sub["unintended"])
244			tq_log.append(sub["torques"][np.argmax(np.abs(sub["torques"]), axis=0), np.arange(6)])
245	
246		return {
247			"t": np.arange(len(q_targets), dtype=np.float64) / float(FPS),
248			"q_cmd": np.array(qcmd_log),
249			"qpos": np.array(qpos_log),
250			"tcp_pos": np.array(tcp_log),
251			"ee_quat": np.array(eeq_log),
252			"brick_pos": np.array(bpos_log),
253			"brick_quat": np.array(bquat_log),
254			"brick_vel": np.array(bvel_log),
255			"brick_ang_vel": np.array(bang_log),
256			"jaw_forces": np.array(jaw_log),
257			"pinch_normal": np.array(jaw_n_log),
258			"pinch_tangential": np.array(jaw_t_log),
259			"unintended_forces": np.array(unint_log),
260			"substep_unintended": np.array(sub_unint_log),
261			"actuator_torques": np.array(tq_log),
262		}

import hashlib, time, math
import numpy as np, mujoco
from digital_twin_armigo.constants import SO101_MJCF_DIR, FPS
from digital_twin_armigo.physics import load_physics_spec
from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import Cell, Layout
from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell.scene import SUBSTEPS
print("FPS", FPS, "SUBSTEPS", SUBSTEPS)
spec = load_physics_spec()
def build():
    lay = Layout(green=(0.26,0.18), pink=(0.26,-0.18), brick_xy=(0.26,0.0), brick_yaw_deg=0.0, defective=True)
    c = Cell(lay, SO101_MJCF_DIR, physics=spec, dynamic_clutter=True, assisted_grasp=False, render_enabled=False)
    c.model.opt.timestep = 1.0/(FPS*SUBSTEPS)
    return c
def fp(m):
    n = mujoco.mj_sizeModel(m); buf = np.zeros(n, np.uint8); mujoco.mj_saveModel(m, None, buf)
    return hashlib.sha256(buf.tobytes()).hexdigest()
c = build(); print("timestep", c.model.opt.timestep, "nq", c.model.nq, "nhistory", getattr(c.model,'nhistory',None), "na", c.model.na, "nplugin", c.model.nplugin)
print("fp", fp(c.model)); c2 = build(); print("fp2", fp(c2.model))
q0 = np.array([0.0,-0.35,0.25,1.35,0.0,1.0])
c.set_joints(q0)
# sweep arm down into brick to create contact
def target(i): 
    s = min(1.0, i/60)
    return q0 + s*np.array([0.0, 0.9, 0.2, -0.3, 0.3, -0.9])
SIG = int(mujoco.mjtState.mjSTATE_INTEGRATION)
n = mujoco.mj_stateSize(c.model, SIG)
t0=time.time()
for i in range(45): c.step_with_telemetry(target(i))
print("45 frames", time.time()-t0, "ncon", c.data.ncon, "brick", c.brick_pos())
st = np.zeros(n); mujoco.mj_getState(c.model, c.data, st, SIG)
for i in range(45,90): c.step_with_telemetry(target(i))
ref = np.zeros(n); mujoco.mj_getState(c.model, c.data, ref, SIG)
def cont(mode):
    d = build(); d.set_joints(q0)
    mujoco.mj_setState(d.model, d.data, st, SIG)
    if mode=="fwd": mujoco.mj_forward(d.model, d.data)
    if mode=="fwd_reset": mujoco.mj_forward(d.model, d.data); mujoco.mj_setState(d.model, d.data, st, SIG)
    for i in range(45,90): d.step_with_telemetry(target(i))
    out = np.zeros(n); mujoco.mj_getState(d.model, d.data, out, SIG); return out
for mode in ("plain","fwd","fwd_reset"):
    o = cont(mode); print(mode, "bit-equal", np.array_equal(o, ref), "maxabs", np.abs(o-ref).max())
# physics-only signature (no warmstart)
SIGP = int(mujoco.mjtState.mjSTATE_FULLPHYSICS)
npz = mujoco.mj_stateSize(c.model, SIGP)
print("sizes", n, npz)
EOF

"""Pinhole camera above the table: pose parametrisation, projection and ray casting. Pure NumPy."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from .constants import PLANE_HEIGHT_M, PLANE_TILT_DEG, TOP_FULL


@dataclass
class CameraPose:
	"""A camera above the table: horizontal position, height, view yaw, tilt from vertical, roll, focal length."""

	x: float
	y: float
	height: float = PLANE_HEIGHT_M
	yaw_deg: float = 0.0
	tilt_deg: float = PLANE_TILT_DEG
	roll_deg: float = 0.0
	focal_px: float = 615.0

	def frame(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
		"""Image right, image up and viewing direction of the camera, as unit vectors in the world."""
		t, p = math.radians(self.tilt_deg), math.radians(self.yaw_deg)
		forward = np.array([math.sin(t) * math.cos(p), math.sin(t) * math.sin(p), -math.cos(t)])
		up = np.array([math.cos(t) * math.cos(p), math.cos(t) * math.sin(p), math.sin(t)])
		right = np.cross(forward, up)
		r = math.radians(self.roll_deg)
		right, up = math.cos(r) * right + math.sin(r) * up, -math.sin(r) * right + math.cos(r) * up
		return right, up, forward

	def axes(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
		"""MuJoCo camera x (image right) and y (image up) axes in the world."""
		right, up, _ = self.frame()
		return right, up

def min_jerk(n: int) -> np.ndarray:
	s = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n)
	return 10 * s**3 - 15 * s**4 + 6 * s**5


class Plan:
	"""Joint targets (radians, one per frame) with a phase label per frame, built from min-jerk segments."""

	def __init__(self, start: np.ndarray, speed: float) -> None:
		self.frames: list[np.ndarray] = []
		self.phases: list[int] = []
		self.last = start.copy()
		self.speed = speed

	def hold(self, secs: float, phase: str) -> None:
		n = round(secs * FPS)
		self.frames.extend([self.last.copy()] * n)
		self.phases.extend([PHASES.index(phase)] * n)

	def move(self, target: np.ndarray, secs: float, phase: str, settle: float = 0.2) -> None:
		n = max(2, int(secs * self.speed * FPS))
		for s in min_jerk(n)[1:]:
			self.frames.append(self.last + s * (target - self.last))
			self.phases.append(PHASES.index(phase))
		self.last = target.copy()
		self.hold(settle, phase)


@dataclass
class Grip:
	"""What the pick decided and the place needs: wrist roll for jaws-down moves and the gripper commands."""

	roll: float
	q_lift: np.ndarray | None = None
	open_g: float = 1.3
	closed_g: float = -0.17

	def __init__(self, start: np.ndarray, speed: float) -> None:
		self.frames: list[np.ndarray] = []
		self.phases: list[int] = []
		self.last = start.copy()
		self.speed = speed

	def hold(self, secs: float, phase: str) -> None:
		n = round(secs * FPS)
		self.frames.extend([self.last.copy()] * n)
		self.phases.extend([PHASES.index(phase)] * n)

	def move(self, target: np.ndarray, secs: float, phase: str, settle: float = 0.2) -> None:
		n = max(2, int(secs * self.speed * FPS))
		for s in min_jerk(n)[1:]:
			self.frames.append(self.last + s * (target - self.last))
			self.phases.append(PHASES.index(phase))
		self.last = target.copy()
		self.hold(settle, phase)

"""Pinhole camera above the table: pose parametrisation, projection and ray casting. Pure NumPy."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from .constants import PLANE_HEIGHT_M, PLANE_TILT_DEG, TOP_FULL


@dataclass
class CameraPose:
	"""A camera above the table: horizontal position, height, view yaw, tilt from vertical, roll, focal length."""

	x: float
	y: float
	height: float = PLANE_HEIGHT_M
	yaw_deg: float = 0.0
	tilt_deg: float = PLANE_TILT_DEG
	roll_deg: float = 0.0
	focal_px: float = 615.0

	def frame(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
		"""Image right, image up and viewing direction of the camera, as unit vectors in the world."""
		t, p = math.radians(self.tilt_deg), math.radians(self.yaw_deg)
		forward = np.array([math.sin(t) * math.cos(p), math.sin(t) * math.sin(p), -math.cos(t)])
		up = np.array([math.cos(t) * math.cos(p), math.cos(t) * math.sin(p), math.sin(t)])
		right = np.cross(forward, up)
		r = math.radians(self.roll_deg)
		right, up = math.cos(r) * right + math.sin(r) * up, -math.sin(r) * right + math.cos(r) * up
		return right, up, forward

	def axes(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
		"""MuJoCo camera x (image right) and y (image up) axes in the world."""
		right, up, _ = self.frame()
		return right, up

def min_jerk(n: int) -> np.ndarray:
	s = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n)
	return 10 * s**3 - 15 * s**4 + 6 * s**5


class Plan:
	"""Joint targets (radians, one per frame) with a phase label per frame, built from min-jerk segments."""

	def __init__(self, start: np.ndarray, speed: float) -> None:
		self.frames: list[np.ndarray] = []
		self.phases: list[int] = []
		self.last = start.copy()
		self.speed = speed

	def hold(self, secs: float, phase: str) -> None:
		n = round(secs * FPS)
		self.frames.extend([self.last.copy()] * n)
		self.phases.extend([PHASES.index(phase)] * n)

	def move(self, target: np.ndarray, secs: float, phase: str, settle: float = 0.2) -> None:
		n = max(2, int(secs * self.speed * FPS))
		for s in min_jerk(n)[1:]:
			self.frames.append(self.last + s * (target - self.last))
			self.phases.append(PHASES.index(phase))
		self.last = target.copy()
		self.hold(settle, phase)

  - `src/digital_twin_armigo/runtime/errors.py` (`LedgerError`, `JobNotFoundError`, `IdempotencyConflictError`, `StaleWorkerError`, `InvalidTransitionError`, `StopLatchedError`)
  - `src/digital_twin_armigo/runtime/canonical.py` (`canonical_json`, `sha256_json`)
- Run tests: `cd /e/digital_twin_armigo && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests/test_runtime_ledger.py -q`

## What to build: `runtime/ledger.py`

An **append-only operation ledger** in one SQLite file. It gives a simulation execution service: idempotent job registration, a job state machine recorded as immutable events, worker leases with monotonically increasing fencing tokens, a per-run stop latch, and budget accounting that cannot be reset. History is never updated or deleted.

### Types
```python
class JobState(StrEnum):
	QUEUED = "QUEUED"
	RUNNING = "RUNNING"
	CANCEL_REQUESTED = "CANCEL_REQUESTED"
	SUCCEEDED = "SUCCEEDED"
	FAILED = "FAILED"
	CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
	NEEDS_RECOVERY = "NEEDS_RECOVERY"

TERMINAL_STATES = frozenset({JobState.SUCCEEDED, JobState.FAILED, JobState.CANCELLED})
```
Frozen dataclasses:
- `JobRecord(job_id: str, idempotency_key: str, op_type: str, params: dict, params_sha256: str, run_id: str, branch_id: str, created_at_utc: str)`
- `JobEvent(seq: int, job_id: str, state: JobState, worker_id: str | None, fencing_token: int | None, payload: dict, created_at_utc: str)`
- `Lease(resource: str, worker_id: str, fencing_token: int)`
- helper `job_resource(job_id: str) -> str` returning `f"job:{job_id}"`.

### `OperationLedger(path: Path)`
Opens/creates the SQLite DB (`journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=FULL`, `busy_timeout` ≥ 5000 ms). One connection with `check_same_thread=False`, `isolation_level=None`, guarded by a `threading.RLock`; every mutating method runs inside an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` … `COMMIT` (ROLLBACK on any exception), so it is safe across threads and across processes that open the same file. Store a schema version in `PRAGMA user_version` (=1); opening a DB with another non-zero version raises `LedgerError`. `close()` and context-manager support.

Tables (suggested):
- `operations(job_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, idempotency_key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, op_type, params_json, params_sha256, run_id, branch_id, created_at_utc)`
- `job_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, job_id, state, worker_id, fencing_token, payload_json, created_at_utc)`
- `lease_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, resource, worker_id, fencing_token INTEGER UNIQUE, created_at_utc)` — the current lease of a resource is its row with the highest `fencing_token`; tokens come from one global counter (max over the whole table + 1, starting at 1), so they are strictly increasing across all resources and never reused, including after reopening the file.
- `stop_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id, action TEXT CHECK(action IN ('LATCH','CLEAR')), reason, actor, created_at_utc)`
- **Append-only enforcement in the database itself**: create `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` triggers on all four tables that `RAISE(ABORT, 'append-only')`.

Methods:

`register(*, idempotency_key: str, op_type: str, params: dict, run_id: str, branch_id: str) -> tuple[JobRecord, bool]`
- `params_sha256 = sha256_json(params)` (params must be canonical-JSON-able; a failure → `LedgerError`).
- New key: if the run's stop latch is set → `StopLatchedError` (nothing written). Otherwise insert the operation with `job_id = uuid.uuid4().hex` plus a first `QUEUED` event, atomically; return `(record, True)`.
- Existing key with the same `op_type`, `params_sha256`, `run_id` and `branch_id` → return `(existing_record, False)` and write nothing (this holds even if the stop latch is set — a retry may always look up its own job).
- Existing key with any of those four different → `IdempotencyConflictError` (nothing written).
- Empty `idempotency_key` → `LedgerError`.

`job(job_id) -> JobRecord`, `job_by_key(idempotency_key) -> JobRecord | None`, `events(job_id) -> list[JobEvent]` (seq order), `latest_event(job_id) -> JobEvent`, `state(job_id) -> JobState`. Unknown job → `JobNotFoundError`.

`acquire_lease(resource: str, worker_id: str) -> Lease` — appends a lease event with the next global token; the previous holder of that resource (if any) is superseded from this moment, even if it is the same `worker_id`.
`current_lease(resource) -> Lease | None`.
`assert_current(lease: Lease) -> None` — `StaleWorkerError` unless `lease` exactly equals the current lease of its resource.

`append_event(job_id: str, state: JobState, *, lease: Lease | None = None, payload: dict | None = None) -> JobEvent`
Allowed transitions (from the job's current state → new state) and who may make them:
- worker-originated — **require** `lease` to be the current lease of `job_resource(job_id)`; otherwise `StaleWorkerError` (missing lease, lease for another resource, or superseded token), checked inside the same transaction as the insert:
  - `QUEUED → RUNNING`
  - `NEEDS_RECOVERY → RUNNING`
  - `RUNNING → SUCCEEDED | FAILED | CANCELLED`
  - `CANCEL_REQUESTED → CANCELLED | SUCCEEDED | FAILED` (a job may finish before it notices the cancel; the truthful outcome is recorded)
- coordinator-originated — `lease` must be `None` (passing one → `LedgerError`):
  - `QUEUED → CANCELLED`
  - `RUNNING → CANCEL_REQUESTED`
  - `RUNNING → NEEDS_RECOVERY`, `CANCEL_REQUESTED → NEEDS_RECOVERY`

`SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA = "snapshot-manifest/v1"`

### `ExperimentIdentity` (frozen dataclass)
Fields (all `str`): `code_sha256`, `assets_sha256`, `config_sha256`, `engine`, `engine_version`, `python_version`, `numpy_version`, `platform`.

### `hash_tree(root: Path, patterns: Sequence[str], exclude: Sequence[str] = ()) -> str`
Deterministic SHA-256 over a file tree: collect files under `root` matching any glob in `patterns` (use `root.glob(pattern)`, files only), drop any whose POSIX relative path matches any `exclude` pattern via `fnmatch.fnmatch`, always drop anything inside a `__pycache__` directory, sort by POSIX relative path, and hash the canonical JSON of the list `[[relpath, sha256_file(path)], ...]`. A missing `root` raises `FileNotFoundError`.

### `current_identity(engine: str, engine_version: str, *, repo_root: Path = REPO_ROOT) -> ExperimentIdentity`
- code: `hash_tree(repo_root / "src" / "digital_twin_armigo", ["**/*.py"])`
- assets: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `{"so101_mjcf": hash_tree(repo_root/"assets"/"so101_mjcf", ["**/*"], exclude=["_sorting_cell_*.xml", "_marker_*.png"]), "meshes": hash_tree(repo_root/"assets"/"meshes", ["**/*"])}`
- config: `hash_tree(repo_root / "config" / "sim", ["**/*"])`
- `python_version = platform.python_version()`, `numpy_version = numpy.__version__`, `platform = platform.platform()`.

### `BlobRef` (frozen dataclass)
`sha256: str`, `size: int`, `kind: str` (`"arrays"` or `"json"`). `to_dict()` / `from_dict()`.

### `SnapshotManifest` (frozen dataclass)
Fields, in this order:
`schema: str`, `snapshot_id: str`, `parent_snapshot_id: str | None`, `run_id: str`, `episode_id: str`, `branch_id: str`, `created_at_utc: str` (ISO-8601 UTC), `control_step: int`, `sim_time_s: float`, `identity: dict[str, str]`, `model_fingerprint: str`, `contract: dict[str, Any]`, `contract_sha256: str`, `scene_spec: dict[str, Any]`, `scene_sha256: str`, `blobs: dict[str, BlobRef]`, `produced_by: dict[str, Any] | None`, `manifest_sha256: str`.
- `body() -> dict` : JSON-able dict of every field EXCEPT `manifest_sha256` (BlobRefs as dicts).
- `to_dict()` : `body()` plus `manifest_sha256`.
- `manifest_sha256` is always `sha256_json(body())`; `contract_sha256 == sha256_json(contract)`; `scene_sha256 == sha256_json(scene_spec)`.

Reject object-dtype arrays and non-str/empty keys with `SnapshotError`. The result must be loadable with `np.load(..., allow_pickle=False)`.
- `put_json(obj: Any) -> BlobRef` — bytes are `canonical_json(obj)` (so NaN/inf raise `ValueError` from the encoder; let that propagate as `SnapshotError`).
- `get_arrays(ref: BlobRef) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]` and `get_json(ref: BlobRef) -> Any` — read the blob file, verify **size and SHA-256 before decoding**; missing file, size mismatch, hash mismatch, wrong `kind`, or a decode failure → `SnapshotCorruptError`.
- Blob file path: `root/blobs/<sha256>`. Write protocol: write bytes to a unique file in `staging/`, `flush` + `os.fsync`, re-read and verify the SHA, then `os.replace` into `blobs/`. If the destination already exists with the right size, skip the move and delete the staging file (dedup). Never leave a partial file in `blobs/`.

Manifest API:
- `commit(*, run_id, episode_id, branch_id, control_step, sim_time_s, identity: ExperimentIdentity, model_fingerprint, contract, scene_spec, blobs: Mapping[str, BlobRef], parent_snapshot_id: str | None = None, produced_by: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, snapshot_id: str | None = None) -> SnapshotManifest`

## What to build: `runtime/ledger.py`

An **append-only operation ledger** in one SQLite file. It gives a simulation execution service: idempotent job registration, a job state machine recorded as immutable events, worker leases with monotonically increasing fencing tokens, a per-run stop latch, and budget accounting that cannot be reset. History is never updated or deleted.

### Types
```python
class JobState(StrEnum):
	QUEUED = "QUEUED"
	RUNNING = "RUNNING"
	CANCEL_REQUESTED = "CANCEL_REQUESTED"
	SUCCEEDED = "SUCCEEDED"
	FAILED = "FAILED"
	CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
	NEEDS_RECOVERY = "NEEDS_RECOVERY"

TERMINAL_STATES = frozenset({JobState.SUCCEEDED, JobState.FAILED, JobState.CANCELLED})
```
Frozen dataclasses:
- `JobRecord(job_id: str, idempotency_key: str, op_type: str, params: dict, params_sha256: str, run_id: str, branch_id: str, created_at_utc: str)`
- `JobEvent(seq: int, job_id: str, state: JobState, worker_id: str | None, fencing_token: int | None, payload: dict, created_at_utc: str)`
- `Lease(resource: str, worker_id: str, fencing_token: int)`
- helper `job_resource(job_id: str) -> str` returning `f"job:{job_id}"`.

### `OperationLedger(path: Path)`
Opens/creates the SQLite DB (`journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=FULL`, `busy_timeout` ≥ 5000 ms). One connection with `check_same_thread=False`, `isolation_level=None`, guarded by a `threading.RLock`; every mutating method runs inside an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` … `COMMIT` (ROLLBACK on any exception), so it is safe across threads and across processes that open the same file. Store a schema version in `PRAGMA user_version` (=1); opening a DB with another non-zero version raises `LedgerError`. `close()` and context-manager support.

Tables (suggested):
- `operations(job_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, idempotency_key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, op_type, params_json, params_sha256, run_id, branch_id, created_at_utc)`
- `job_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, job_id, state, worker_id, fencing_token, payload_json, created_at_utc)`
- `lease_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, resource, worker_id, fencing_token INTEGER UNIQUE, created_at_utc)` — the current lease of a resource is its row with the highest `fencing_token`; tokens come from one global counter (max over the whole table + 1, starting at 1), so they are strictly increasing across all resources and never reused, including after reopening the file.
- `stop_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id, action TEXT CHECK(action IN ('LATCH','CLEAR')), reason, actor, created_at_utc)`
- **Append-only enforcement in the database itself**: create `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` triggers on all four tables that `RAISE(ABORT, 'append-only')`.

Methods:

`register(*, idempotency_key: str, op_type: str, params: dict, run_id: str, branch_id: str) -> tuple[JobRecord, bool]`
- `params_sha256 = sha256_json(params)` (params must be canonical-JSON-able; a failure → `LedgerError`).
- New key: if the run's stop latch is set → `StopLatchedError` (nothing written). Otherwise insert the operation with `job_id = uuid.uuid4().hex` plus a first `QUEUED` event, atomically; return `(record, True)`.
- Existing key with the same `op_type`, `params_sha256`, `run_id` and `branch_id` → return `(existing_record, False)` and write nothing (this holds even if the stop latch is set — a retry may always look up its own job).
- Existing key with any of those four different → `IdempotencyConflictError` (nothing written).
- Empty `idempotency_key` → `LedgerError`.

`job(job_id) -> JobRecord`, `job_by_key(idempotency_key) -> JobRecord | None`, `events(job_id) -> list[JobEvent]` (seq order), `latest_event(job_id) -> JobEvent`, `state(job_id) -> JobState`. Unknown job → `JobNotFoundError`.

`acquire_lease(resource: str, worker_id: str) -> Lease` — appends a lease event with the next global token; the previous holder of that resource (if any) is superseded from this moment, even if it is the same `worker_id`.
`current_lease(resource) -> Lease | None`.
`assert_current(lease: Lease) -> None` — `StaleWorkerError` unless `lease` exactly equals the current lease of its resource.

`append_event(job_id: str, state: JobState, *, lease: Lease | None = None, payload: dict | None = None) -> JobEvent`
Allowed transitions (from the job's current state → new state) and who may make them:
- worker-originated — **require** `lease` to be the current lease of `job_resource(job_id)`; otherwise `StaleWorkerError` (missing lease, lease for another resource, or superseded token), checked inside the same transaction as the insert:

  - `NEEDS_RECOVERY → RUNNING`
  - `RUNNING → SUCCEEDED | FAILED | CANCELLED`
  - `CANCEL_REQUESTED → CANCELLED | SUCCEEDED | FAILED` (a job may finish before it notices the cancel; the truthful outcome is recorded)
- coordinator-originated — `lease` must be `None` (passing one → `LedgerError`):
  - `QUEUED → CANCELLED`
  - `RUNNING → CANCEL_REQUESTED`
  - `RUNNING → NEEDS_RECOVERY`, `CANCEL_REQUESTED → NEEDS_RECOVERY`
  - `NEEDS_RECOVERY → SUCCEEDED | FAILED` (recovery adopted or rejected an already-written result)
- Everything else, including any transition out of a terminal state and any `X → X`, → `InvalidTransitionError`. `QUEUED` can never be appended (only `register` writes it).
- The event row stores `worker_id`/`fencing_token` from the lease (NULL for coordinator events) and `payload` as canonical JSON (default `{}`).
- Stop latch: `QUEUED → RUNNING` and `NEEDS_RECOVERY → RUNNING` raise `StopLatchedError` while the job's run is latched. Finishing transitions are still allowed while latched.

`request_cancel(job_id: str, *, reason: str = "") -> JobState` — idempotent convenience: `QUEUED → CANCELLED`; `RUNNING → CANCEL_REQUESTED`; `CANCEL_REQUESTED`, `NEEDS_RECOVERY` or terminal → no write; returns the resulting current state. Payload `{"reason": reason}`.

`incomplete_jobs(run_id: str | None = None) -> list[JobRecord]` — jobs whose current state is not terminal, oldest first.

Stop latch: `latch_stop(run_id, *, reason: str, actor: str) -> None`, `clear_stop(run_id, *, reason: str, actor: str) -> None`, `stop_latched(run_id) -> bool` (true iff the latest stop event for the run is `LATCH`), `stop_history(run_id) -> list[dict]`. `clear_stop` requires non-empty `reason` and `actor` (`LedgerError` otherwise) and raises `LedgerError` if the run is not latched. Latching an already-latched run appends another LATCH event (allowed). `consumed(run_id: str) -> dict[str, float | int]` — budget accounting derived only from the append-only history, covering **every branch** of the run:
`{"operations": <number of registered operations for the run>, "attempts": <number of RUNNING events>, "sim_time_s": <sum of payload["sim_time_consumed_s"] over all events of the run's jobs that carry that key>, "wall_time_s": <same for payload["wall_time_s"]>}`.

Fencing: tokens strictly increase across different resources and across close/reopen of the DB file; after a second `acquire_lease` on the same resource, the first lease gets `StaleWorkerError` on `append_event(... SUCCEEDED ...)` and on `assert_current`, and **no event row is written**; a lease for job A cannot move job B; a worker transition with `lease=None` raises `StaleWorkerError`.

11. You are implementing ONE self-contained module in the Python repo at `E:/digital_twin_armigo` (Windows; use the Bash tool with POSIX paths like `/e/digital_twin_armigo`). Work test-first (write the failing tests, watch them fail, then implement).

## Hard rules
- Create ONLY these two files: `src/digital_twin_armigo/runtime/ledger.py` and `tests/test_runtime_ledger.py`. Do not modify, format, or delete any other file. No git commands that change anything.
- Code style: **tabs for indentation**, line length 120, `from __future__ import annotations`, Python >= 3.12, type hints, short docstrings. Stdlib only (`sqlite3`, `json`, `uuid`, `threading`, `datetime`, `enum`, `dataclasses`).
- Reuse existing helpers; read them first:
  - `src/digital_twin_armigo/runtime/errors.py` (`LedgerError`, `JobNotFoundError`, `IdempotencyConflictError`, `StaleWorkerError`, `InvalidTransitionError`, `StopLatchedError`)
  - `src/digital_twin_armigo/runtime/canonical.py` (`canonical_json`, `sha256_json`)
- Run tests: `cd /e/digital_twin_armigo && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests/test_runtime_ledger.py -q`
- Before finishing both must be clean: `.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff check src/digital_twin_armigo/runtime/ledger.py tests/test_runtime_ledger.py` and `.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff format src/digital_twin_armigo/runtime/ledger.py tests/test_runtime_ledger.py`
- Tests use pytest `tmp_path`, need no MuJoCo, and the whole file should run in well under 10 s.

## What to build: `runtime/ledger.py`

An **append-only operation ledger** in one SQLite file. It gives a simulation execution service: idempotent job registration, a job state machine recorded as immutable events, worker leases with monotonically increasing fencing tokens, a per-run stop latch, and budget accounting that cannot be reset. History is never updated or deleted.

### Types
```python
class JobState(StrEnum):
	QUEUED = "QUEUED"
	RUNNING = "RUNNING"
	CANCEL_REQUESTED = "CANCEL_REQUESTED"
	SUCCEEDED = "SUCCEEDED"
	FAILED = "FAILED"
	CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
	NEEDS_RECOVERY = "NEEDS_RECOVERY"

TERMINAL_STATES = frozenset({JobState.SUCCEEDED, JobState.FAILED, JobState.CANCELLED})
```
Frozen dataclasses:
- `JobRecord(job_id: str, idempotency_key: str, op_type: str, params: dict, params_sha256: str, run_id: str, branch_id: str, created_at_utc: str)`
- `JobEvent(seq: int, job_id: str, state: JobState, worker_id: str | None, fencing_token: int | None, payload: dict, created_at_utc: str)`
- `Lease(resource: str, worker_id: str, fencing_token: int)`
- helper `job_resource(job_id: str) -> str` returning `f"job:{job_id}"`.

### `OperationLedger(path: Path)`
Opens/creates the SQLite DB (`journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=FULL`, `busy_timeout` ≥ 5000 ms). One connection with `check_same_thread=False`, `isolation_level=None`, guarded by a `threading.RLock`; every mutating method runs inside an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` … `COMMIT` (ROLLBACK on any exception), so it is safe across threads and across processes that open the same file. Store a schema version in `PRAGMA user_version` (=1); opening a DB with another non-zero version raises `LedgerError`. `close()` and context-manager support.

Tables (suggested):
- `operations(job_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, idempotency_key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, op_type, params_json, params_sha256, run_id, branch_id, created_at_utc)`
- `job_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, job_id, state, worker_id, fencing_token, payload_json, created_at_utc)`
- `lease_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, resource, worker_id, fencing_token INTEGER UNIQUE, created_at_utc)` — the current lease of a resource is its row with the highest `fencing_token`; tokens come from one global counter (max over the whole table + 1, starting at 1), so they are strictly increasing across all resources and never reused, including after reopening the file.
- `stop_events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id, action TEXT CHECK(action IN ('LATCH','CLEAR')), reason, actor, created_at_utc)`
- **Append-only enforcement in the database itself**: create `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` triggers on all four tables that `RAISE(ABORT, 'append-only')`.

Methods:

`register(*, idempotency_key: str, op_type: str, params: dict, run_id: str, branch_id: str) -> tuple[JobRecord, bool]`
- `params_sha256 = sha256_json(params)` (params must be canonical-JSON-able; a failure → `LedgerError`).
- New key: if the run's stop latch is set → `StopLatchedError` (nothing written). Otherwise insert the operation with `job_id = uuid.uuid4().hex` plus a first `QUEUED` event, atomically; return `(record, True)`.
- Existing key with the same `op_type`, `params_sha256`, `run_id` and `branch_id` → return `(existing_record, False)` and write nothing (this holds even if the stop latch is set — a retry may always look up its own job).
- Existing key with any of those four different → `IdempotencyConflictError` (nothing written).
- Empty `idempotency_key` → `LedgerError`.

`job(job_id) -> JobRecord`, `job_by_key(idempotency_key) -> JobRecord | None`, `events(job_id) -> list[JobEvent]` (seq order), `latest_event(job_id) -> JobEvent`, `state(job_id) -> JobState`. Unknown job → `JobNotFoundError`.

`acquire_lease(resource: str, worker_id: str) -> Lease` — appends a lease event with the next global token; the previous holder of that resource (if any) is superseded from this moment, even if it is the same `worker_id`.
`current_lease(resource) -> Lease | None`.
`assert_current(lease: Lease) -> None` — `StaleWorkerError` unless `lease` exactly equals the current lease of its resource.

`append_event(job_id: str, state: JobState, *, lease: Lease | None = None, payload: dict | None = None) -> JobEvent`
Allowed transitions (from the job's current state → new state) and who may make them:
- worker-originated — **require** `lease` to be the current lease of `job_resource(job_id)`; otherwise `StaleWorkerError` (missing lease, lease for another resource, or superseded token), checked inside the same transaction as the insert:
  - `QUEUED → RUNNING`
  - `NEEDS_RECOVERY → RUNNING`
  - `RUNNING → SUCCEEDED | FAILED | CANCELLED`
  - `CANCEL_REQUESTED → CANCELLED | SUCCEEDED | FAILED` (a job may finish before it notices the cancel; the truthful outcome is recorded)
- coordinator-originated — `lease` must be `None` (passing one → `LedgerError`):
  - `QUEUED → CANCELLED`
  - `RUNNING → CANCEL_REQUESTED`
  - `RUNNING → NEEDS_RECOVERY`, `CANCEL_REQUESTED → NEEDS_RECOVERY`
  - `NEEDS_RECOVERY → SUCCEEDED | FAILED` (recovery adopted or rejected an already-written result)
- Everything else, including any transition out of a terminal state and any `X → X`, → `InvalidTransitionError`. `QUEUED` can never be appended (only `register` writes it).
- The event row stores `worker_id`/`fencing_token` from the lease (NULL for coordinator events) and `payload` as canonical JSON (default `{}`).
- Stop latch: `QUEUED → RUNNING` and `NEEDS_RECOVERY → RUNNING` raise `StopLatchedError` while the job's run is latched. Finishing transitions are still allowed while latched.

`request_cancel(job_id: str, *, reason: str = "") -> JobState` — idempotent convenience: `QUEUED → CANCELLED`; `RUNNING → CANCEL_REQUESTED`; `CANCEL_REQUESTED`, `NEEDS_RECOVERY` or terminal → no write; returns the resulting current state. Payload `{"reason": reason}`.

`incomplete_jobs(run_id: str | None = None) -> list[JobRecord]` — jobs whose current state is not terminal, oldest first.

Stop latch: `latch_stop(run_id, *, reason: str, actor: str) -> None`, `clear_stop(run_id, *, reason: str, actor: str) -> None`, `stop_latched(run_id) -> bool` (true iff the latest stop event for the run is `LATCH`), `stop_history(run_id) -> list[dict]`. `clear_stop` requires non-empty `reason` and `actor` (`LedgerError` otherwise) and raises `LedgerError` if the run is not latched. Latching an already-latched run appends another LATCH event (allowed). Nothing else in the ledger ever clears a latch: reopening the file, registering, acquiring leases, or appending events must leave it set.

`consumed(run_id: str) -> dict[str, float | int]` — budget accounting derived only from the append-only history, covering **every branch** of the run:
`{"operations": <number of registered operations for the run>, "attempts": <number of RUNNING events>, "sim_time_s": <sum of payload["sim_time_consumed_s"] over all events of the run's jobs that carry that key>, "wall_time_s": <same for payload["wall_time_s"]>}`.

## Tests required in `tests/test_runtime_ledger.py` (at minimum)
1. register creates a job in `QUEUED`; same key + same params returns the same `job_id` with `created=False` and no new rows; key reuse with different params / op_type / run_id / branch_id each raise `IdempotencyConflictError` and write nothing; params key order does not matter (`{"a":1,"b":2}` vs `{"b":2,"a":1}` is the same request).
2. Happy path `QUEUED → RUNNING → SUCCEEDED` with a lease; events carry worker id + token + payload; terminal states reject every further transition (parametrize over all states).
3. Fencing: tokens strictly increase across different resources and across close/reopen of the DB file; after a second `acquire_lease` on the same resource, the first lease gets `StaleWorkerError` on `append_event(... SUCCEEDED ...)` and on `assert_current`, and **no event row is written**; a lease for job A cannot move job B; a worker transition with `lease=None` raises `StaleWorkerError`.
4. The full transition table: every allowed transition succeeds with the right originator, and every other (from, to) pair raises `InvalidTransitionError` (build it by parametrizing over `JobState × JobState`).
5. Cancel: queued → `CANCELLED`; running → `CANCEL_REQUESTED` then worker `CANCELLED`; cancel-requested job that completes records `SUCCEEDED`; `request_cancel` on a terminal job is a no-op returning the terminal state; calling it twice writes one event.
6. Recovery path: `RUNNING → NEEDS_RECOVERY` (coordinator) → new lease → `RUNNING → SUCCEEDED`; the old lease is rejected throughout; also `NEEDS_RECOVERY → SUCCEEDED` by the coordinator with a payload.
7. Append-only: raw `UPDATE` and `DELETE` statements against each of the four tables through a separate `sqlite3.connect` to the same file raise `sqlite3.DatabaseError`/`IntegrityError` and leave row counts unchanged.
8. Stop latch: latched run refuses new `register` (`StopLatchedError`) but returns an existing job for a retried key; refuses `QUEUED → RUNNING`; allows a running job to finish; survives close/reopen; `clear_stop` needs reason+actor and then work is accepted again; latch on run A does not affect run B; history lists LATCH and CLEAR in order.
9. Budget: `consumed` sums across two branches of the same run, counts attempts including a re-run after `NEEDS_RECOVERY`, ignores other runs, and is unchanged by close/reopen.
10. Durability/atomicity: after close and reopen all jobs, events and states are identical; a failing transition inside `append_event` leaves the ledger unchanged; opening a DB whose `user_version` is 99 raises `LedgerError`.
11. Concurrency: 8 threads calling `register` with the same key and same params all get the same `job_id` and exactly one reports `created=True`; 8 threads racing `acquire_lease` on one resource get 8 distinct tokens and only the highest passes `assert_current`. Also two `OperationLedger` instances opened on the same file see each other's writes.

## Report back (keep it short)
State: tests added (count) and the exact final pytest summary line, ruff check + format results, and any place you deviated from this spec or found it ambiguous. Do not paste the code.

S="$TEMP/claude/c7b4122de520ed7e/904ca024-aa79-43d8-83e7-1fe27d5c9d21/scratchpad" && cat > "$S/probe2.py" <<'EOF'
import math, time
import numpy as np, mujoco
from digital_twin_armigo.constants import SO101_MJCF_DIR, FPS, REST_U
from digital_twin_armigo.joints import normalized_to_rad
from digital_twin_armigo.physics import load_physics_spec
from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import Cell, Layout, Plan, best_roll, ik
spec = load_physics_spec()
SUB=8
def build(assisted=False):
    lay = Layout(green=(0.26,0.18), pink=(0.26,-0.18), brick_xy=(0.26,0.0), brick_yaw_deg=0.0, defective=True)
    c = Cell(lay, SO101_MJCF_DIR, physics=spec, dynamic_clutter=True, assisted_grasp=assisted, render_enabled=False)
    c.model.opt.timestep = 1.0/(FPS*SUB)
    return c
OPEN_G, HOLD_G = 0.85, 0.06
c = build()
q_start = normalized_to_rad(np.array(REST_U, dtype=np.float64)); q_start[5]=OPEN_G
c.set_joints(q_start)
size = c.layout.brick_size; bx,by = 0.26,0.0
short_axis = np.array([0.0,1.0])
q_hover = ik(c, np.array([bx,by,0.09]), q_start.copy(), 0.0)
roll, sign = best_roll(c, q_hover, short_axis)
off = -sign*short_axis*(size[1]/2+0.006); gx,gy = bx+off[0], by+off[1]
plan = Plan(q_start, 1.0); plan.hold(0.3,"rest")
q = np.array([0.0,-0.35,0.25,1.35,0.0,OPEN_G]); plan.move(q,0.8,"approach")
marks={}
for x,y,z,g,secs,ph in ((gx,gy,0.09,OPEN_G,1.4,"approach"),(gx,gy,0.026,OPEN_G,1.2,"approach"),(gx,gy,0.006,OPEN_G,0.7,"grasp"),(gx,gy,0.006,HOLD_G,1.0,"grasp"),(gx,gy,0.12,HOLD_G,1.2,"lift")):
    q = ik(c, np.array([x,y,z]), q, roll); q[5]=g; plan.move(q,secs,ph)
marks['lifted']=len(plan.frames)
q2=q.copy(); q2[5]=OPEN_G; plan.move(q2,0.4,"place"); plan.hold(0.6,"place")
T=np.array(plan.frames); print("frames",len(T),marks)
c.set_joints(q_start); c.data.qvel[:]=0
c.set_brick_pose(np.array([bx,by,size[2]/2+0.0005]), np.array([0,0,0,1.0]))
c.data.ctrl[:6]=q_start
for _ in range(12): mujoco.mj_step(c.model,c.data)
t0=time.time()
for i,t in enumerate(T):
    sub=c.step_with_telemetry(t, SUB)
    if i%15==0 or i>marks['lifted']-3:
        lv,av=c.brick_vel()
        if i%15==0 or i<marks['lifted']+25: print(i, "z=%.4f"%c.brick_pos()[2], "jaw", np.round(sub["jaw_total"][-1],2), "v=%.3f"%np.linalg.norm(lv), "g=%.2f"%t[5])
print("time",time.time()-t0)
# warmstart negative control
SIG=int(mujoco.mjtState.mjSTATE_INTEGRATION)
n=mujoco.mj_stateSize(c.model,SIG)
def run(k0,k1,cell):
    for t in T[k0:k1]: cell.step_with_telemetry(t,SUB)
def fresh():
    d=build(); d.set_joints(q_start); d.data.qvel[:]=0
    d.set_brick_pose(np.array([bx,by,size[2]/2+0.0005]), np.array([0,0,0,1.0])); d.data.ctrl[:6]=q_start
    for _ in range(12): mujoco.mj_step(d.model,d.data)
    return d
a=fresh(); k=marks['lifted']-20; run(0,k,a)
st=np.zeros(n); mujoco.mj_getState(a.model,a.data,st,SIG)
ws=a.data.qacc_warmstart.copy(); print("warmstart norm", np.linalg.norm(ws))
run(k,k+40,a); ref=np.zeros(n); mujoco.mj_getState(a.model,a.data,ref,SIG)
b=fresh(); mujoco.mj_setState(b.model,b.data,st,SIG); run(k,k+40,b); o=np.zeros(n); mujoco.mj_getState(b.model,b.data,o,SIG); print("full", np.array_equal(o,ref))
b=fresh(); mujoco.mj_setState(b.model,b.data,st,SIG); b.data.qacc_warmstart[:]=0; run(k,k+40,b); o=np.zeros(n); mujoco.mj_getState(b.model,b.data,o,SIG); print("no-warmstart equal?", np.array_equal(o,ref), np.abs(o-ref).max())
b=fresh(); b.data.qpos[:]=a.data.qpos*0+st[1:14] if False else b.data.qpos
EOF

from digital_twin_armigo.physics import load_physics_spec
from digital_twin_armigo.mujoco_cell import Cell, Layout, Plan, best_roll, ik
spec = load_physics_spec(); SUB=8; OPEN_G=0.85
lay = Layout(green=(0.26,0.18), pink=(0.26,-0.18), brick_xy=(0.26,0.0), brick_yaw_deg=0.0, defective=True)
c = Cell(lay, SO101_MJCF_DIR, physics=spec, dynamic_clutter=True, assisted_grasp=False, render_enabled=False)
c.model.opt.timestep = 1.0/(FPS*SUB)
q_start = normalized_to_rad(np.array(REST_U, dtype=np.float64)); q_start[5]=OPEN_G
size = lay.brick_size; bx,by = 0.26,0.0
def trial(off_m, z_grip, hold_g, verbose=False):
    c.set_joints(q_start)
    q_hover = ik(c, np.array([bx,by,0.09]), q_start.copy(), 0.0)
    roll, sign = best_roll(c, q_hover, np.array([0.0,1.0]))
    off = -sign*np.array([0.0,1.0])*off_m; gx,gy=bx+off[0],by+off[1]
    plan = Plan(q_start,1.0); plan.hold(0.3,"rest")
    q = np.array([0.0,-0.35,0.25,1.35,0.0,OPEN_G]); plan.move(q,0.8,"approach")
    for x,y,z,g,secs,ph in ((gx,gy,0.09,OPEN_G,1.4,"approach"),(gx,gy,z_grip+0.02,OPEN_G,1.2,"approach"),(gx,gy,z_grip,OPEN_G,0.7,"grasp"),(gx,gy,z_grip,hold_g,1.0,"grasp"),(gx,gy,0.12,hold_g,1.2,"lift")):
        q = ik(c, np.array([x,y,z]), q, roll); q[5]=g; plan.move(q,secs,ph)
    T=np.array(plan.frames)
    c.data.qvel[:]=0; c.set_joints(q_start)
    c.set_brick_pose(np.array([bx,by,size[2]/2+0.0005]), np.array([0,0,0,1.0])); c.data.ctrl[:6]=q_start
    mujoco.mj_resetData  # noqa
    for _ in range(12): mujoco.mj_step(c.model,c.data)
    for t in T: sub=c.step_with_telemetry(t,SUB)
    return c.brick_pos()[2], sub["jaw_total"][-1], len(T)
for off_m, z, g in itertools.product((0.0, 0.006, 0.012, 0.0159+0.006, 0.03), (0.006, 0.012, 0.02), (0.06, -0.1)):
    bz, jaw, n = trial(off_m, z, g)
    print(f"off={off_m:.4f} z={z:.3f} g={g:+.2f} -> brick z={bz:.4f} jaw={np.round(jaw,2)} n={n}")
EOF

287					np.lib.format.write_array(entry, np.asarray(arrays[key], order="C"), allow_pickle=False)
288					info = zipfile.ZipInfo(f"{key}.npy", date_time=(1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0))
289					info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_STORED
290					zf.writestr(info, entry.getvalue())
291			return self._put_bytes(buf.getvalue(), "arrays")

293		def put_json(self, obj: Any) -> BlobRef:
294			"""Store ``obj`` as canonical JSON."""
295			try:
296				data = canonical_json(obj)
297			except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
298				raise SnapshotError(f"object is not canonically JSON-encodable: {exc}") from exc
299			return self._put_bytes(data, "json")

301		def _read_verified(self, ref: BlobRef) -> bytes:
302			path = self.blobs_dir / ref.sha256
303			try:
304				data = path.read_bytes()
305			except OSError as exc:
306				raise SnapshotCorruptError(f"blob {ref.sha256} is missing or unreadable") from exc
307			if len(data) != ref.size:
308				raise SnapshotCorruptError(f"blob {ref.sha256} has size {len(data)}, expected {ref.size}")
309			if sha256_bytes(data) != ref.sha256:
310				raise SnapshotCorruptError(f"blob {ref.sha256} fails its SHA-256 check")
311			return data
